takeaway: Typical rainy-season Friday for northern Pacific Costa Rica: partly cloudy mornings, afternoon showers and storms, and a chance of coastal rain at night. Hot inland (about 35°C in Nicoya, 36.5°C in Liberia). Surf winds stay onshore from the Pacific — choppier faces, not classic easterly glass. Hurricane Polo is Category 5 well off southwestern Mexico; another system may form near Tehuantepec later and track along southern Mexico — nothing near Costa Rica. Prolonged multi-day rain watch is elevated but not locked in. A tropical wave this weekend could bump Saturday–Sunday afternoon rains a bit.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Fri–Sun)
periods.pattern: Morning partly cloudy; afternoon scattered showers and storms; night rain possible along the coast. Light-to-moderate rain chances overall. Winds stay Pacific/onshore. Near Papagayo: light winds, seas about 4–6 ft; a brief overnight easterly Friday night, then south/southwest again.
periods.implications: Use mornings outdoors. For surf, prefer overnight and early-morning lulls — not all-day glass. Watch Sat–Sun if the weekend tropical wave makes afternoons wetter.
periods.confidence: High that storms stay local/seasonal and no nearby cyclone. Moderate on exact Nosara timing and amounts.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Mon–Thu)
periods.pattern: Slight easing of Pacific rains early next week, with isolated afternoon storms still possible. Winds remain mostly Pacific/onshore. Seas stay moderate; Papagayo often light or variable midweek.
periods.implications: Keep late-day plans flexible Mon–Wed. Surf still onshore-side — no clean trade return on the main model picture.
periods.confidence: Moderate for continued showers; low–moderate for a true multi-day temporales.

periods.label: Days 8–15
periods.pattern: Longer-range outlook still leans drier than normal for the northern Pacific into early October. No signal for a prolonged flood-season spike on the Nicoya coast, though short heavy cells can still pop.
periods.implications: No official prolonged wet spell flagged for Nicoya Pacific. Treat any single wet day as a short cell, not a new season pattern.
periods.confidence: Moderate for the quieter theme; low for day-by-day detail.

gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Roughly Saturday through Tuesday (26–29 Sep) while Pacific moisture and the weekend tropical wave overlap
gyreWatch.supporting: Models keep moist Pacific flow into Nicoya through the weekend into early next week. Costa Rica’s weekend tropical wave could add afternoon rain Sat–Sun. A system near southern Mexico may add more Pacific moisture. One model family is a bit wetter midweek than the others.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No closed gyre over Central America — the pattern is moist Pacific flow and distant Mexico systems, not a Costa Rica-centered rain machine. Distant hurricanes stay off Mexico. Average model rain for Nicoya looks mostly light-to-moderate. Official longer-range outlook still leans drier from late September.

surfWinds.detail: Low-level flow is from the Pacific side (southwest/west), which chops west-facing Nosara beaches. Nicaragua is not showing all-day offshore trades either, so don’t expect Nosara all-day glass. A short overnight easterly near Papagayo Friday night may help local night glass, then daytime onshore returns.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Overnight and early morning Fri–Sun. No clean all-day offshore signal this weekend.
surfWinds.confidence: High on the overall onshore pattern for the next week; moderate on exact hour-to-hour lulls.

whatChanged: Today’s Costa Rica forecast puts more afternoon storm language on the northern Pacific and allows coastal rain at night. The weekly now highlights Tropical Wave #47 for Sat–Sun. Polo is back to Category 5 farther west; Tehuantepec formation odds are higher (~90%). Wind picture unchanged: still Pacific onshore, not trades.
practical: Best outdoors: mornings before afternoon storms. Expect heat inland and possible night rain on the coast. For surf, chase night and early-morning lulls — not all-day glass. Keep an eye on Sat–Tue if the weekend wave and Pacific moisture verify wetter. Latest storm aviso was Thursday evening (Nicoya-focused); no new Friday aviso yet.
